convergence.seed_protocol: SeedSequence(root).spawn(budgets * 2 * n_seeds); budget/method/replicate order; uint64 child seeds
convergence.stream_design: Fresh independent pseudorandom streams for each budget, method, and replicate; no shared draws
convergence.interval_method: estimate +/- 1.96 * sample standard error; paired means for antithetic
convergence.cost_model: Equal discounted-payoff evaluations: N plain normals versus N/2 antithetic normals and N/2 independent pairs; excludes runtime and RNG costs

portfolio_calibration.data_source: Generated synthetic price CSV; no market observations
limitations: Historical close-to-close covariance is used as a constant scenario and pricing volatility proxy; it is not an implied volatility surface.
The drift remains the fixed 3% rate, not an estimated physical expected return. These are model scenarios, not validated real-world tail probabilities.
252 equal trading steps per year are assumed; supply consecutive synchronized adjusted daily closes. No holiday, split or dividend adjustment is inferred.
Gaussian GBM discards skewness, heavy tails and volatility clustering, even when present in the input CSV. Calibration does not validate this model.
Twelve scramble changes measure numerical variability only; parameter uncertainty and out-of-sample accuracy are unmeasured.

provenance.data: Call benchmark: synthetic risk-neutral GBM; portfolio comparison records its own dated CSV provenance

limitations: Normal approximation confidence intervals, not finite-sample guarantees.
Coverage and RMSE have sampling uncertainty across a finite set of seeds; no calibration or monotonic convergence guarantee.
One synthetic option parameter setting; equal payoff counts do not establish a runtime speedup.
The call benchmark is classical; the studio's separate discrete quantum example does not estimate portfolio tail risk.
CSV calibration uses constant historical covariance with risk-neutral drift; it does not establish real-world tail accuracy.
